passages.quote:
You’ll get a letter or email if someone applies to court to claim you owe them money. You must respond by the date on the email or letter you receive.

Follow the instructions in the email or letter.

The process is different in Scotland.

This guide is also available in Welsh (Cymraeg).

Ways to respond

You can:

pay the full amount

offer to pay a different amount (if you think you owe less than the claim amount)

defend the claim (if you do not think you owe any money)

You may have to give more information at a court hearing if you offer to pay a different amount and it’s rejected, or if you defend the claim.

You may not have to attend a court hearing if:

the claimant withdraws their claim

you reach an agreement directly with the claimant

you work out an agreement through mediation

You can also make a claim against them (‘counterclaim’) if you think they owe you money. You might have to pay a court fee.

If you need more time to respond

If you need more time to respond you can ask for:

an extra 14 days if you’re responding by post

an extra 28 days if you’re responding online

You might get a county court judgment (CCJ) or have to pay more if you do not respond in time.

Get advice

You may be able to get free legal advice about your case from Advicenow.
